checks.evidence: deduplicate discards a head that appears in the original tail, hence keeps final occurrences; it does not sort. The output finite set is built from the list and the proved Nodup evidence.

JL044 covers all lists over any type with DecidableEq, including empty input and repeated values. The second named contract JL044_members checks every x and every xs, independently fixing membership semantics.
Only DecidableEq α is required. The main Nodup theorem does not assume distinct input; the separate unchanged-output theorem explicitly requires xs.Nodup.

The main conclusion is Nodup, and the membership contract also prevents dropping all input elements from satisfying the stated broader preservation goal. Length nonincrease and idempotence are proved. The specification explicitly excludes a standalone stability or complexity theorem.

The membership induction handles dropped and retained heads. When retaining x, its absence from the original tail transfers through mem_deduplicate to absence from the deduplicated tail, giving nodup_cons. Idempotence follows by applying preservation of already-Nodup lists.
